findings.explanation: The instance defines exactly one cluster block, so there is no cross-zone/cross-region replication. A zonal outage in var.cluster.zone takes the whole instance down, and there is no automatic failover. Originally not fixable because holden had no operator to express a repeated-block cardinality check.
findings.remediation: Resolved: added an optional dynamic "cluster" block over var.replica_clusters (defaults to [], so existing single-cluster callers are unaffected). Upstream holden gained a count_gte operator and shipped it as HLD_GCP_344, which correctly evaluates the derived cluster count against the module's own default and fails there — suppressed at google_bigtable_instance.tf with mechanism-based reasoning (holden can't resolve variable values through the dynamic block for any caller). A second, local policy (HLD_PROPOSED_003, .holden/policies/bigtable-module-call-ha.yaml) checks the module CALL's own replica_clusters argument instead, which needs no such resolution: it correctly fails on module.bigtable (single-cluster, suppressed there with a call-site-specific reason) and passes on module.bigtable_ha (real replica configured, example/examplea/module.bigtable.tf), demonstrating the capability end-to-end.
findings.title: Bigtable instance has only a single cluster (no replication)

findings.explanation: google_kms_crypto_key_iam_binding is authoritative: it replaces the entire IAM policy for the role on the key, not just adds to it. var.kms_key_id is passed in from outside the module (see example/examplea/module.bigtable.tf), so the key is very likely shared with other consumers. Any other principal granted cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on that key outside this module's state will be silently revoked on the next apply, which can break unrelated services using the same CMEK key.
findings.remediation: Switch to google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member, which only adds this module's binding and leaves any other bindings on the key untouched.
findings.title: Authoritative IAM binding used on a KMS key this module does not own

findings.explanation: Same authoritative-binding failure class as HOLDEN_BP_002. The table is created by this module, so risk is lower today, but google_bigtable_table_iam_binding still replaces the entire member list for roles/bigtable.user on that table. If any other Terraform config or team ever grants roles/bigtable.user to a different principal on the same table (a realistic pattern for a shared analytics/application datastore), this resource silently revokes it on next apply. Holden's own HLD_GCP_330 already flags the identical pattern for project/folder/org-scoped bindings; it doesn't yet extend to table scope.
findings.fix:
resource "google_bigtable_table_iam_member" "editor" {
  for_each      = google_bigtable_table.table_resource
  table         = each.value.name
  instance_name = google_bigtable_instance.pike.name
  role          = "roles/bigtable.user"
  member        = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.bigtable.email}"
}
findings.remediation: Switch to google_bigtable_table_iam_member, additive per member, no collision risk.
findings.title: Authoritative IAM binding used on a table, latent collision risk with any other IAM grant on the same table

findings.explanation: There is no required_providers/required_version block anywhere in the root module (only example/examplea/terraform.tf pins one). Author's call: version constraints are intentionally kept out of this reusable module and only declared in the implementing/root configuration (as example/examplea/terraform.tf already does), so callers control their own provider range. Not a gap.
findings.title: Root module has no provider version constraints

findings.explanation: cpu_target and storage_target are declared as `string` in the cluster object type, but google_bigtable_instance's autoscaling_config expects both as `number` (cpu_target is a percentage 10-80, storage_target is GB). Terraform's implicit string<->number conversion currently papers over this, but the declared type doesn't match what the field actually holds (example/examplea passes them as bare numbers), which is misleading to module consumers.
findings.remediation: Change both fields to `number` in the cluster object type.
findings.title: autoscaling_config.cpu_target/storage_target typed as string but consumed as numbers
